title: Three serial filters leave ocean damping unresolved in an SST-only model
abstract: We test whether corrected SST persistence can identify ocean damping. In a daily linear model, persistent forcing, ocean response and analysis smoothing form three serial filters. Six assignments of distinct time constants give identical SST paths. Joint SST-product comparisons retain a common-factor ambiguity. With early roots of 1, 3 and 20 days and late roots of 3, 8 and 20 days, fixed forcing still permits ocean-time ratios from 0.4 to 20. External bounds can resolve the labels. We give an enumeration tool and a two-proxy moment design that identifies damping under independent measurement errors. In 200 noisy synthetic 44-year records, its median time is 20.85 days for a true 20 days, but seven estimates are invalid and the valid estimates have a wide range. Shared proxy error and buoy filtering each cause rejection in all 200 tests. This extends a known two-factor ambiguity; it does not fit real SST or establish an observed damping trend.

display.caption: Exact SST correlation ambiguity, permitted ocean histories, and two-proxy measurement tests. All values are synthetic.
